purpose: Test a certificate-aware attacker that corrupts sampled poison identities after the protected draw, and compare an uncorrected certificate with the declared-B robust certificate.
attack_knowledge: the sampled records' true adjudicated identities
the sampled records' frozen detector flags
the certificate formula, tau, alpha cap, and delta
attack_timing: after the secret draw and before aggregate adjudication counts are released
optimizer: enumerate all feasible allocations of at most B helpful flips and select GO first, then the largest recall lower margin, then the largest clean-rate margin, then the fewest flips
comparators: naive certificate that assumes B=0 on corrupted counts
robust certificate evaluated with the true declared corruption bound B
primary_endpoint: false-GO rate among detector decisions whose true recall is below tau or whose true clean flag rate exceeds alpha cap
secondary_endpoints: fraction of previously non-GO decisions converted to GO
robust-certificate GO, NO-GO, and ABSTAIN rates
minimum corruption rate producing a false GO in each block and detector

claim_rule.expected: The naive B=0 certificate may fail under label corruption. The robust certificate must produce zero false GO whenever the declared B covers the attack.
claim_rule.failure: Any robust false GO is a load-bearing implementation or theorem discrepancy and blocks the claim.

scope: This red team violates perfect adjudication but does not reveal or influence the protected sample before the draw. It does not test key compromise, population replacement, or an underestimated B.
